newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end firmer on hint of colder weather.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end firmer on hint of colder weather.

text.p: FCOJ futures bounced back from their oversold state as a hint of cold weather on the horizon helped to fuel the modest recovery, traders said.

"Some of the weather forecasters talked about a hint of cold weather in the citrus belt around 21-22 January," Bernard Savaiko of PaineWebber said. "This spooked some of the shorts to cover. It was a technical bounce from an oversold condition."
Forecaster Mike Palmerino of Weather Services Corp said there was a suggestion of colder weather later in the month. "But right now it looks like it won't be cold enough to produce any damage."
Citrus belt temperatures were unlikely to dip below 32 to 36 degrees Farenheit, Palmerino added.

With the cold weather hinted for January, the spot month contract leaped 2.25 cents higher to close at 76.35 cents per pound, while most active March futures went out 1.90 cents firmer at 79.55 cents.
Volume was estimated at 2,291 lots compared to Friday's 2,650 lots.
Despite some recovery, prices are still some 20 cents down on where they were in late November.
